help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The unknown woman is said to have been his former colleague from the embassy. (others say)
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Mrs Albers herself claims to have seen the two of them together in a café on the market square in the spring. (she says so herself)
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The claim comes from other people, so it is soll. will would mean he claims it himself; muss would be the narrator's own firm conclusion.
help.tips[0].en.text: soll relays what other people say (the rumours in the building); will relays what the subject says about himself or herself, and signals that the narrator does not vouch for it. Both keep the claim at a distance — the difference is who is speaking.
help.tips[0].en.title: Who is the source? soll vs will
help.tips[0].en.trap: will + Infinitiv II is not "wants to have": Er will … gearbeitet haben = he claims to have worked. And don't double the hearsay: Man sagt, er soll … is redundant — soll already means "people say".
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Anyone who gets up so early and goes to bed so late must be tremendously disciplined. (firm conclusion)
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: It can't be a mistake; the letters come too regularly for that. (ruled out)
help.tips[1].examples[2].en: That may well be true, I sometimes think. (concession before an "aber")
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: dürfte expresses ‘probably’, an estimate. muss is a firm conclusion, and will / soll report what someone says.
help.tips[1].en.text: muss (a firm conclusion) > dürfte (probably) > könnte / kann (possibly) > mag (conceding: "that may well be so, but …") > kann nicht (ruled out). The narrator's evidence decides the step: a strict routine → muss; an estimate → dürfte; one explanation among others → könnte; a letter that comes every week → kann nicht.
help.tips[1].en.title: How sure is the narrator? The certainty scale
help.tips[1].en.trap: dürfte here is not "would be allowed to" but "probably"; könnte is not ability but possibility.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: The boxes of books he carried down to the cellar probably weighed several hundred kilos altogether.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: So he might have spent a long time abroad.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: A guess about the past keeps the modal now and puts Partizip II + sein at the end: gewesen sein (sein takes sein).
help.tips[2].en.text: The supposition is made now, about then: the modal stays in the present (or the Konjunktiv II for dürfte / könnte), and the past moves into the infinitive — Partizip II + haben / sein at the very end.
help.tips[2].en.title: Past supposition: modal now + Infinitiv II
help.tips[2].en.trap: Not "Er hat im Ausland verbringen können" — that is objective ability (he was able to). The supposition needs the Infinitiv II.
help.hookEn: Who is the mysterious tenant on the third floor? Follow the rumours and learn to say exactly how sure you are.
help.introEn: A new tenant on the third floor, a narrator who watches him, and a building full of talk: the story sorts every statement about the man by its source and by how sure the speaker is. What the neighbours pass on is hearsay (soll); what the man and Frau Albers say about themselves is a claim the narrator keeps at arm's length (will); what the narrator concludes from the evidence — the early mornings, the heavy book boxes, the grey letters with a coat of arms, the fluent Russian — runs down the certainty scale from sure to ruled out. Twelve gaps, each hint giving only the English meaning (people say, he claims, surely, probably, possibly, may well, impossible, hardly likely). Six of the gaps are about the past: the modal stays in the present and the Infinitiv II follows (gelebt haben, gewogen haben, verbracht haben, gewesen sein, gesehen haben, gearbeitet haben). Read to the end first — the final scene with the parcel resolves the tension.
help.rememberEn[0]: soll = other people say it; will = the subject says it about himself. Certainty: muss > dürfte > könnte > mag > kann nicht.
help.rememberEn[1]: Past supposition: modal in the present + Partizip II + haben / sein (soll gelebt haben, dürften gewogen haben).
